description: Backend Medium and Low findings cluster, all verifiable with vitest/tsc/eslint. Covers M-1, M-2, M-4, M-5, M-6, M-3 (deferral/doc), L-1, L-2, L-3, L-4, L-5. Make one atomic, user-authored commit per finding (or per tightly-related pair). All backend-only; depends on FEAT-002 only to avoid touching the same WS files concurrently. Where a finding is 'report vs implement', make the smallest correct change the audit endorses and note the choice in the commit message and the feature findings.
steps: COMMIT (M-1): Fastify route JSON schemas vs the dead err.validation branch. The design (.kiro/specs/threshold-doorbell/design.md §9 'every route validated against its Fastify JSON schema') and .kiro/steering/tech.md ('Schema-validated routes') mandate route schemas, but no route in backend/src/routes/*.ts declares a `schema:` option, so the err.validation branch in app.ts is dead code. Choose the smallest correct change the audit endorses: EITHER (a) add Fastify JSON schemas (body/querystring/params) to the routes so the validation contract is real and the schema_validation_failure metric fires through app.ts's err.validation branch (keep existing service-layer hand-validation as defense-in-depth; ensure error envelopes still map to the 'schema' code and 400 — note Fastify's default validation error has err.validation set, which app.ts already converts to errors.schema()); OR (b) if adding schemas to every route risks destabilizing the hand-validation and tests, amend design.md §9 and steering/tech.md to state validation is service-layer by explicit choice AND remove the now-provably-dead err.validation branch in app.ts (and its test, if any). Prefer (a) for at least the simplest routes (e.g. POST /replies, POST /transcripts querystring/body, GET /transcripts querystring) if feasible without breaking tests; otherwise (b). Document which path was taken and why. If (a): add a test asserting a schema violation returns 400 code 'schema' and increments schema_validation_failure. If (b): the removal must be covered by noting no route declares a schema.

COMMIT (M-2): bound request field sizes below the 64 KiB body limit. backend/src/routes/replies.ts accepts visitorText as any string; backend/src/services/transcript-service.ts accepts a turns array with no item cap and each turn.text with no length cap. Add an explicit maxLength on visitorText and turn.text and a maxItems cap on turns. If M-1 was done via route schemas, express these as maxLength/maxItems in those schemas. Otherwise add explicit service-layer checks that return errors.schema() (400) when visitorText exceeds a few KiB (choose a sane cap, e.g. 4096 chars), when turns exceeds a bounded count (e.g. 500), or when any turn.text exceeds a cap (e.g. 2048 chars). Keep the global 64 KiB bodyLimit. Add tests: an over-long visitorText -> 400 schema; an over-long turns array / turn.text -> 400 schema; a normal payload still 201/200. This directly completes the FEAT-004 step E item that added bodyLimit but not maxLength/maxItems.

COMMIT (M-5): backend/.env.example documents only the original variables and ships insecure defaults, and its comment lists `local | staging | demo` while config.ts also supports `test`. Update .env.example to document EVERY variable config.ts reads: THRESHOLD_ENV (note it accepts local|staging|demo|test, with staging/demo requiring real 32+ char secrets), PORT, HOST, SESSION_SECRET (note: must be a strong 32+ char secret outside local/test), RING_CLIENT_ID/RING_CLIENT_SECRET/RING_AUTHORIZE_URL/RING_TOKEN_URL/RING_REDIRECT_URI/RING_API_BASE, APP_DEEP_LINK, WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY, WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEYS (comma-separated rotation list, newest first), WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated; EMPTY by default means browser WS clients cannot connect — call this out as the common misdiagnosis), BODY_LIMIT_BYTES, RATE_LIMIT_MAX, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS, WS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, ASR_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RESIDENT, ASR_MAX_SESSION_MS, ASR_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS, ASR_MAX_PENDING_FRAMES, KMS_KEY_ID. Keep the local-fixture defaults for local but add an explicit note that staging/demo boot fails fast (assertStrongSecret) if the insecure defaults or short secrets are used. This is a docs-only edit (no code). No new test; the existing config.test.ts covers config behavior.

COMMIT (M-6): latency metrics observe() is defined but never recorded. backend/src/observability/metrics.ts defines LatencyMetric incl 'webhook_ack_ms' and the g-series, but grep shows no metrics.observe(...) call in routes/services. Record at least webhook_ack_ms in the webhook route (backend/src/routes/webhook.ts): capture a start time at handler entry and call app.container.metrics.observe('webhook_ack_ms', elapsedMs) right before/after sending the 200 ack (the ack is sent before the async push, so measure to the ack). Reason about the g-series: g1a/g1b/g2/g3 are largely app-side latencies (open-to-first-caption, tap-to-audio) that belong to the app latency harness, so for the backend wire only what the backend can actually observe (webhook_ack_ms, and optionally feed the onResponse hook's reply.elapsedTime into a generic observe if a suitable metric exists — do NOT invent new metric names outside the LatencyMetric union). In the commit message and feature findings, note which metrics are now wired server-side and that the remaining g-series are app-side (per design §10). Add/extend a test in backend/test/observability/metrics-wiring.test.ts (it already exists) asserting webhook_ack_ms is observed after a valid signed webhook delivery (use buildTestApp, compute a valid timestamped HMAC with t.config.webhookHmacKey, POST /webhook, then assert t.metrics.latency('webhook_ack_ms') is non-null with count>=1).

COMMIT (M-4): /ready readiness probe is shallow. backend/src/app.ts runReadinessChecks only checks typeof config.env === 'string' and that tokenStore.get('__readiness_probe__') does not throw (in fixture mode it never throws, so readiness == liveness). Make the readiness checks adapter-driven in a way that is still green in fixture mode but would catch a broken real datastore: keep the fixture path returning ready, but structure runReadinessChecks so each dependency check (tokenStore, and any datastore the container exposes) is an awaited probe with a per-check timeout so a hung real adapter fails the check rather than hanging /ready. Add a bounded Promise.race timeout (e.g. 1000ms) around each check. Do NOT fabricate adapters that do not exist; the point is to make the structure correct and documented so a real adapter's failing probe surfaces as not-ready. Update the comment to reflect the timeout. Add a test asserting /ready returns 200 with all checks ok in fixture mode, and (optionally) a test injecting a tokenStore whose get() rejects, asserting /ready returns 503 with the tokenStore check ok:false (buildTestApp accepts a tokenStore override via ContainerOverrides).

COMMIT (M-3 deferral note): the per-resident ASR cap (asr.ts liveByResident) and single-session invariant (signaling-service.ts active map) are per-process only. This is already documented as deferred in both files and in .agents/tasks/task-audit-remediation/features/FEAT-004.json. Do NOT implement a shared store (no Redis/DynamoDB adapter exists). Instead, make the deferral explicit in the design spec: add an entry under design.md §12 'Known open items' (see the design/spec-drift commit) OR confirm the existing in-code DEFERRED comments reference the correct tracking location. The actual spec §12 edit is handled in FEAT-005's doc commit; here, verify the code comments in asr.ts and signaling-service.ts accurately describe the cross-instance limitation and the shared-store remediation, and tighten the wording only if inaccurate. If no code change is needed, record M-3 as 'documented, deferred' in the findings and skip a code commit (do not create an empty commit).

COMMIT (L-4): backend/src/services/ring-token-service.ts getAccessToken treats an unparseable expiresAt (NaN) as 'not near expiry' (nearExpiry = Number.isFinite(expiresMs) && ...), so a corrupt record skips refresh and tries to return a possibly-expired token. Change the logic so a non-finite expiresMs forces a refresh: compute `const expiresMs = Date.parse(record.expiresAt); const mustRefresh = !Number.isFinite(expiresMs) || expiresMs - now <= REFRESH_SKEW_MS;` and branch on mustRefresh (refresh when true, decrypt-and-return when false). Preserve the MED-31 single-flight refresh and the decrypt-error -> refresh_failed mapping. Add a test in backend/test/services/ring-token-service.test.ts: a stored record with expiresAt='not-a-date' (or '') triggers a refresh (assert the ring.refresh path runs / new tokens persisted) rather than returning the stale access token.

COMMIT (L-2 + L-3): webhook host allowlist breadth and timestamp requirement. (L-2) backend/src/services/webhook-service.ts ALLOWED_THUMBNAIL_HOST_SUFFIXES = ['.ring.com', '.amazonaws.com'] — '.amazonaws.com' is very broad. Since the exact Ring/S3 bucket host is not known yet, the audit's endorsed smallest change is to document WHY the broad suffix is currently acceptable (webhook is HMAC-authenticated; sanitizer already requires HTTPS) in a clear code comment, OR narrow it if a specific host is identifiable from the fixtures/spec (check backend/src/services/fixtures and design.md for any concrete thumbnail host; if none, keep the suffix and document). (L-3) backend/src/security/hmac.ts verifyTimestampedSignature requires an x-ring-timestamp header and signs timestamp.body; if real Ring webhooks differ, every real delivery would 401. This only matters when the real integration lands and the format is unknown today. The endorsed change is to DOCUMENT the assumption clearly: add a comment at the webhook route (backend/src/routes/webhook.ts) and/or hmac.ts stating the signing contract (timestamp header present, HMAC over `timestamp.body`, +/-5min window) MUST be validated against Ring's actual Partner webhook spec before go-live, and that verifySignature (body-only) remains available as the fallback scheme. Both L-2 and L-3 are documentation/comment changes (no behavior change, no new test); keep them in one commit as a 'webhook contract documentation' cluster. Do NOT weaken the existing anti-replay or allowlist behavior.

COMMIT (L-5): backend/src/services/webhook-service.ts quarantines events for an unmapped device under UNMAPPED_RESIDENT='__unmapped__'; these rows are never attributable to a real resident and are not removed by any resident's DELETE /me/data, relying solely on the 7-day event TTL. The audit endorses EITHER re-attributing __unmapped__ events on first device mapping OR documenting that unmapped events live only until the TTL and are intentionally unerasable per-resident. Choose the documentation path (smallest correct change; re-attribution requires a mapping hook and store scan that is out of scope for a per-process fixture): add a clear comment at UNMAPPED_RESIDENT and in the device-mapping path explaining the retention/erasure semantics (quarantined under an explicit marker, never pushed, removed only by the 7-day TTL, not attributable to a per-resident erasure, and that a future device-mapping event SHOULD re-attribute). If a device-mapping entry point exists (deviceAccountStore.map) and re-attribution is trivially safe in the fixture, prefer implementing it with a test; otherwise document and record the choice. No behavior regression to the __unmapped__ quarantine (it must still never be pushed).

COMMIT (L-1): HSTS and the `secure` cookie flag are keyed on `env !== 'local'` (app.ts onSend HSTS; oauth.ts secure: config.env !== 'local' at ~4 sites) rather than on actual TLS. The audit endorses either deriving 'is this connection secure' from x-forwarded-proto/request.protocol where available, OR documenting that all non-local envs are guaranteed TLS at the edge. Choose the smallest correct change: add a clear comment at the HSTS onSend hook in app.ts and near the oauth.ts cookie `secure` flags stating the deployment invariant (every non-local env terminates TLS at the edge, per design §11) so the env-name coupling is intentional and documented; optionally add a small helper that prefers x-forwarded-proto === 'https' when the header is present and falls back to env !== 'local'. Do not change behavior for local/test. If a helper is added, add a test; if documentation-only, note the choice. Keep the diff minimal and do not regress the secure/sameSite cookie attributes.

After each commit, run `export PATH=/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH && cd backend && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test` and confirm green before moving to the next finding. Author every commit as the user: `git -c user.name="Suleiman" -c user.email="85356587+suletetes@users.noreply.github.com" commit -m "..."`. Stage only the files for that finding (git add specific paths). No em/en dashes in any message, comment, or doc.
acceptance_criteria: M-1: either route-level Fastify JSON schemas exist and a schema violation returns 400 code 'schema' (and the err.validation branch is now reachable/tested), or design.md §9 + steering/tech.md are amended to service-layer validation by choice and the dead err.validation branch is removed; the chosen path is documented.

M-2: visitorText has a maxLength, turns has a maxItems cap, and turn.text has a maxLength (via schema or explicit service check); over-limit inputs return 400 'schema' and are covered by tests; normal payloads still succeed.

M-5: backend/.env.example documents every variable config.ts reads (including WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEYS, WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS with its empty-default caveat, the ASR/rate-limit/body-limit knobs, and that THRESHOLD_ENV accepts test) with safe placeholders and a staging/demo strong-secret note.

M-6: webhook_ack_ms (and any other backend-observable latency metric) is recorded via metrics.observe on the request path, with a test asserting it is observed; the commit message notes which g-series metrics remain app-side.
M-4: runReadinessChecks is adapter-driven with a per-check timeout, returns ready in fixture mode, and would surface a failing/hung dependency as 503; covered by a test.
M-3: the per-process cap limitation is accurately documented in code comments and tracked in the spec (via FEAT-005's §12 edit); recorded as documented/deferred.
L-4: a non-finite expiresAt forces a refresh (mustRefresh) instead of returning a stale token; covered by a test.
L-2/L-3: the thumbnail host allowlist breadth and the webhook timestamp/signing-contract assumptions are clearly documented (or narrowed where a concrete host is known), with no behavior regression.
L-5: __unmapped__ event retention/erasure semantics are documented (or re-attribution implemented with a test), with the quarantine still never pushed.
L-1: the HSTS/secure-flag env coupling is documented as an intentional TLS-at-edge invariant (or derived from x-forwarded-proto), with no change to local/test behavior.
backend npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm run test all pass after every commit; commits are atomic (one finding/cluster each) and authored by Suleiman.
verification: export PATH=/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH && cd backend && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test
findings:
All backend Medium and Low findings addressed. Baseline after FEAT-002 was 279 tests across 37 files; now 288 tests across 37 files (9 new tests). typecheck, lint, and test all green after every commit. 8 atomic, user-authored (Suleiman) commits on fix/audit-findings-remediation (M-3 needed no code change, no commit). No pushes or PRs.

M-1 (commit ae908e3, 'remove dead err.validation branch; document service-layer validation'): RESOLUTION = approach (b). Attempted approach (a) first by adding a Fastify body schema to POST /replies, but Fastify runs body/query validation BEFORE the preHandler (the requireSession guard), so an unauthenticated no-body POST returned 400 (validation) instead of 401 (auth), breaking the existing auth-first test contract ('requires a session'). Verified via a standalone Fastify repro (no-body POST with a body schema -> 400 before preHandler). Since any required-body route schema reorders auth vs validation and the suite asserts auth-first, chose (b): removed the provably-dead err.validation branch in backend/src/app.ts (no route declares a schema, so err.validation never fires; a framework-level 4xx is still mapped to a 'schema' envelope by the generic client-error branch below it) and amended .kiro/specs/threshold-doorbell/design.md section 9 to state validation is service-layer by explicit choice with the auth-first rationale. schema_validation_failure is still incremented via the AppError('schema') branch that errors.schema() throws from the service layer (metrics-wiring test still passes). Edited only design.md section 9 per briefing scope; did not touch design.md section 1 table / structure.md (out of scope). File refs: backend/src/app.ts error handler; design.md section 9.

M-2 (commit 0808a44, 'bound visitorText, turns count, and turn.text sizes'): service-layer caps returning errors.schema() (400). visitorText <= 4096 chars (backend/src/routes/replies.ts MAX_VISITOR_TEXT_CHARS), turns <= 500 items (backend/src/services/transcript-service.ts MAX_TURNS_PER_TRANSCRIPT, checked before map), turn.text <= 2048 chars (MAX_TURN_TEXT_CHARS in parseTurn). Global 64 KiB bodyLimit kept. Tests added: replies.test.ts over-long visitorText -> 400 schema and at-cap -> 200; transcripts.test.ts over-long turns array -> 400, over-long turn.text -> 400, at-cap turns count -> 201, at-cap turn.text -> 201 (boundary tests kept under the 64 KiB body limit by not combining both maxima in one payload). +5 tests.

M-5 (commit 648a6f6, docs-only): backend/.env.example now documents every variable config.ts reads (THRESHOLD_ENV incl test, PORT, HOST, SESSION_SECRET, RING_* set, APP_DEEP_LINK, WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY, WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEYS rotation list newest-first, WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS with the empty-default-blocks-browser-WS caveat, BODY_LIMIT_BYTES, RATE_LIMIT_MAX, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS, WS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, ASR_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RESIDENT, ASR_MAX_SESSION_MS, ASR_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS, ASR_MAX_PENDING_FRAMES, KMS_KEY_ID) with local-fixture defaults and a staging/demo fail-fast strong-secret note. No code, no new test (config.test.ts unchanged and green).

M-6 (commit aeadf1f, 'record webhook_ack_ms latency'): backend/src/routes/webhook.ts captures performance.now() at handler entry and calls app.container.metrics.observe('webhook_ack_ms', elapsed) right before the 200 ack (ack precedes the async push, so it measures the SLA-relevant latency). No new metric names invented (webhook_ack_ms is in the LatencyMetric union). The g-series (g1a/g1b/g2/g3) are app-side open-to-first-caption and tap-to-audio latencies per design.md section 10 and are intentionally left to the app harness; noted in the commit. Test added in backend/test/observability/metrics-wiring.test.ts asserting latency('webhook_ack_ms').count >= 1 after a valid signed delivery. +1 test.

M-4 (commit afaa2a7, 'adapter-driven readiness with per-check timeout'): backend/src/app.ts runReadinessChecks now wraps each dependency probe in timedCheck() which races the probe against READINESS_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 1000ms; a rejected or timed-out probe yields ok:false (503), while the in-process fixture probe resolves immediately (ready). The config check stays synchronous. Did not fabricate adapters. Test added in backend/test/app/error-and-headers.test.ts: injected a tokenStore whose get() rejects via buildContainer({tokenStore}) + buildApp, asserting /ready -> 503 with tokenStore check ok:false; the existing fixture-ready test still passes. +1 test.

M-3 (NO COMMIT - documented, deferred): verified the in-code DEFERRED comments in backend/src/routes/asr.ts (liveByResident per-process map, HIGH-22 cap) and backend/src/services/signaling-service.ts (active per-process map, FR-4.7 single-session invariant). Both already accurately describe the cross-instance limitation (per-process only; a resident could hold the cap/one session PER instance across a multi-pod deployment) and the shared-store remediation (atomic DynamoDB/Redis counter / conditional-write claim row or distributed lock keyed by residentSub), and both reference the tracking location (.agents/tasks/task-audit-remediation/features/FEAT-004.json). No tightening needed; no empty commit created. The spec section 12 'Known open items' edit is owned by FEAT-005, not here.

L-4 (commit eb71acd, 'force refresh on unparseable expiresAt'): backend/src/services/ring-token-service.ts getAccessToken now computes mustRefresh = !Number.isFinite(expiresMs) || expiresMs - now <= REFRESH_SKEW_MS and refreshes when true, so a corrupt expiresAt (NaN) forces a refresh instead of returning a stale token. MED-31 single-flight and the decrypt-error -> refresh_failed mapping preserved. Test added asserting expiresAt='not-a-date' triggers the refresh path (ring.refreshInvocations === 1, fresh access- token returned). +1 test.

L-2 + L-3 (commit e1f83a1, docs-only, single cluster): RESOLUTION = documentation (no concrete Ring/S3 thumbnail host exists in fixtures or design, and Ring's real webhook signing format is unknown here). L-2: comment at ALLOWED_THUMBNAIL_HOST_SUFFIXES in backend/src/services/webhook-service.ts explaining the broad .amazonaws.com suffix is acceptable today (HMAC-authenticated webhook + https-only sanitizer) and MUST be narrowed to the specific Ring S3 bucket host before go-live. L-3: comment at the webhook route verification block in backend/src/routes/webhook.ts stating the ASSUMED signing contract (x-ring-timestamp present, HMAC over timestamp.body, +/-5 min window) MUST be validated against Ring's actual Partner webhook spec before go-live, and that body-only verifySignature remains the fallback. No behavior change; anti-replay and allowlist untouched; no new test.

L-5 (commit 188097c, docs-only): RESOLUTION = documentation (re-attribution needs an event-store scan-and-rewrite by deviceId that EventStorePort does not expose). Comments added at UNMAPPED_RESIDENT in backend/src/services/webhook-service.ts and at the device-mapping path (mapAll) in backend/src/routes/devices.ts explaining that quarantined events are never pushed, not attributable to a resident, not removed by DELETE /me/data, removed only by the 7-day TTL, and that a future device-mapping event SHOULD re-attribute. Quarantine still never pushes; no behavior change; no new test.

L-1 (commit 1b70e61, docs-only): RESOLUTION = documentation of the TLS-at-edge deployment invariant. Comments added at the HSTS onSend hook in backend/src/app.ts and above registerOAuthRoutes in backend/src/routes/oauth.ts (covering all four cookie secure flags) explaining that keying on env !== 'local' is intentional because every non-local env terminates TLS at the edge (design.md sections 5 and 11), that deriving the flag from request.protocol would wrongly drop HSTS/secure behind a TLS-terminating proxy, and noting the x-forwarded-proto fallback for a future topology. No change to local/test behavior and no change to secure/sameSite attributes; no new test.

Security/architecture strengths preserved: PKCE, HKDF key separation, envelope crypto, constant-time compares, recursive log redaction, fail-closed boot, MED-34 WS Origin check, HIGH-22 ASR guards, the FEAT-002 WS revocation fix. No em/en dashes used in any code, comment, doc, or commit message. No Flutter/app/README/design-section-12 edits (reserved for FEAT-004/FEAT-005).
